correctness.rationale: For selected p clique and q independent vertices, the maximal path order is min(p+q,2p+1). The closed star of a chosen leaf is a cone; outside it, exactly the t-1-vertex critical facets with p>=ceil((t-1)/2) survive, and all their proper faces lie in the cone. Collapsing the cone yields the stated sphere wedge with the exact integer multiplicity. The leaf-fixed relative integral chain complex gives signed exterior-power modules without denominator or torsion. The augmented-chain Hopf trace formula gives the full cycle-type character. Since p>=2 for t>=5, every pth exterior-power summand has zero S_r invariants by a transposition sign. Independent graph DFS and bitset homology tests passed 41 parameter cases; signed traces passed 880 automorphisms, 310 leaf stabilizers and five full-group averages. Limits: the finite tests are corroboration only; general claims rest on symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The complete split graph is a canonical chordal graph family with a forbidden-path constraint directly motivated by 2026 multipartite work. The result uniformly classifies all t>=5 and all clique/leaf part sizes, with natural sphere multiplicities and integral symmetry lattices. The full S_r x S_n character determines actions moving the particular leaf used to construct the wedge, which the nonequivariant Betti numbers and leaf-stabilizer lattice do not alone present. Global invariant homology vanishes for all parameters despite arbitrary positive ranks, a genuinely equivariant structural distinction. This is a complete natural family calculation, not an arbitrary finite case, minor numerical refinement, or mere substitution into a known table.
